PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeSat
3-SAT.

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
    clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

TARGET = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-lh5ooi1x && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Clique.

Standard construction:
  * For every clause and every literal position in it, create one vertex.
    Vertices are grouped by clause: vertex 3*c + p corresponds to the p-th
    literal of clause c.
  * Add an edge between two vertices from different clauses exactly when
    their literals are not complementary (i.e. not v and -v).  Vertices in
    the same clause are never adjacent.
  * Set k = number of clauses.

A clique of size k must pick exactly one vertex from each of the k clauses,
and pairwise non-complementarity means the chosen literals can all be made
true simultaneously, yielding a satisfying assignment.  Conversely, any
satisfying assignment gives one true literal per clause, and those vertices
are pairwise adjacent.  A formula with no clauses maps to k = 0, which the
Clique problem answers yes, matching the empty 3-SAT formula.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    n = 3 * len(clauses)
    edges = []

    # literal of vertex 3*c + p
    def literal(c, p):
        return clauses[c][p]

    for c1 in range(len(clauses)):
        for c2 in range(c1 + 1, len(clauses)):
            for p1 in range(3):
                l1 = literal(c1, p1)
                for p2 in range(3):
                    l2 = literal(c2, p2)
                    # Complementary literals cannot both be true.
                    if l1 != -l2:
                        edges.append([3 * c1 + p1, 3 * c2 + p2])

    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": len(clauses)}
EOF
